issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose purchase has not been completed or crystallized is not protected from termination under the special provisions for armed-forces landlords merely because the tenant became a deemed purchaser.
material_facts: The landlord’s application to resume the agricultural land was dismissed, resulting in the tenant becoming a deemed purchaser.
Proceedings to determine the purchase price were later dropped because the landlord was a minor, and the tenant did not challenge that decision.
After attaining majority, the landlord joined the armed forces and later gave notice terminating the tenancy under the special provisions for armed-forces landlords.
The tenant’s purchase rights had not been crystallized when the landlord sought to terminate the tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was only a deemed purchaser, not a completed purchaser, so the exclusion for land purchased by a tenant did not prevent the armed-forces landlord from terminating the tenancy and seeking possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 43-1B and 43-1E of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, the special termination power for an armed-forces landlord overrides preceding provisions, while the exclusion for land purchased by a tenant applies to a completed purchase and not merely deemed-purchaser status where purchase rights have not crystallized. The Court applied the Bombay High Court’s reasoning in Bhimrao Tatoba Sawant v. Heramb Anant Patwardhan.

rule.if: armed_forces_tenancy_termination_proceeding and landlord_is_armed_forces_member and tenant_has_only_deemed_purchase_status and tenant_purchase_rights_not_crystallized

predicates.armed_forces_tenancy_termination_proceed: The proceeding concerns an armed-forces landlord seeking to terminate a tenancy and recover agricultural land.
predicates.landlord_is_armed_forces_member: The landlord is a serving or former member of the armed forces.
predicates.tenant_has_only_deemed_purchase_status: The tenant is treated as a purchaser by operation of law but has not completed a purchase.
predicates.tenant_purchase_rights_not_crystallized: The tenant’s rights as purchaser have not become settled through completion of the purchase process.
predicates.armed_forces_landlord_may_terminate_tena: The armed-forces landlord may terminate the tenancy and seek possession of the land.

issues.definition: When an armed-forces landlord seeks to terminate a tenancy and the tenant has only deemed-purchaser status without crystallized purchase rights, the landlord may terminate the tenancy and seek possession.

issues.legal_issue: An unchallenged final decision of a tribunal binds the parties even if the decision may have been legally incorrect, and cannot be disregarded in later proceedings.
material_facts: The tribunal dropped the purchase-price proceedings on the ground that the landlord was then a minor.
The tenant did not challenge the tribunal’s decision, which became final.
In later proceedings, the tenant argued that the tribunal should not have dropped the purchase-price proceedings and that the tenant should be treated as a purchaser.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal’s final decision bound both parties and could not be treated as having no legal effect merely because it might have been wrong.
issues.legal_principle: A decision does not become a nullity simply because it may be erroneous; it continues to bind the parties unless it is set aside. The respondent relied on Nago Dattu Mahajan v. Smt. Yeshodabai Huna Mahajan concerning a landlord’s choice between resumption procedures, but the Court held that the unchallenged tribunal decision could not be ignored. The dispute arose in the context of Sections 31, 31G, and 32G of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948.

rule.if: later_tenancy_proceeding and tribunal_order_final and party_did_not_challenge_order and party_seeks_to_disregard_order

predicates.later_tenancy_proceeding: A later proceeding concerns rights arising from an earlier tribunal decision about a tenancy or purchase of land.
predicates.tribunal_order_final: The tribunal’s decision has become final and has not been set aside.
predicates.party_did_not_challenge_order: A party bound by the tribunal’s decision did not challenge it.
predicates.party_seeks_to_disregard_order: A party later argues that the tribunal’s decision should have no effect because it was wrong.
predicates.final_tribunal_order_binds_the_parties: The final tribunal decision continues to bind the parties unless it is set aside.

issues.definition: In a later tenancy proceeding, a party cannot disregard a final tribunal order that the party did not challenge, even by arguing that the order was wrong.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who does not use an available opportunity to give the required intimation does not thereby acquire completed purchaser status and remains a tenant whose tenancy may be terminated.
material_facts: The tenant was given an additional opportunity to give intimation to the landlord and the tribunal to exercise the purchase right concerning land held from a landlord who had been a minor.
The tenant did not use that opportunity.
The tenant therefore continued as a tenant when the armed-forces landlord sought to terminate the tenancy.
issues.conclusion: Because the tenant did not use the additional opportunity to give intimation, the tenant remained a tenant and the tenancy could be terminated under the special provisions for armed-forces landlords.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31F(1A) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 provided an additional opportunity for a tenant holding land from a minor landlord to give intimation of the exercise of the purchase right. The Court noted that the tenant did not use that opportunity and continued as a tenant.

predicates.tenant_purchase_opportunity_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s opportunity to exercise a right to purchase land held from a landlord who had been a minor.
predicates.tenant_was_given_additional_intimation_o: The tenant was given an additional opportunity to notify the landlord and the relevant authority of the intention to exercise the purchase right.
predicates.tenant_did_not_give_intimation: The tenant did not provide the required intimation within the available opportunity.
predicates.tenant_remains_terminable_tenant: The tenant remains a tenant whose tenancy may be terminated.

issues.definition: When a tenant is given an additional opportunity to give notice of exercising a purchase right but does not do so, the tenant remains a terminable tenant.
